baseHint.dim: Minor third and diminished fifth: tense
baseHint.aug: Major third and augmented fifth: suspense, mystery
baseHint.sus2: Second instead of third: open and modern
baseHint.sus4: Fourth instead of third: hanging, wants to resolve

seventhHint.b7: Minor seventh: bluesy; with a major third it's the classic dominant
seventhHint.maj7: Major seventh: soft, dreamy, jazz and bossa
seventhHint.dim7: Diminished seventh: very tense, symmetric, thriller-movie sound

extHint.b9: ♭9: dark, dramatic tension; typical on dominants (G7♭9 → C)
extHint.9: 9: the friendliest color: softens and modernizes any chord
extHint.#9: ♯9: the 'Hendrix' chord: major and minor at once, blues and rock
extHint.11: 11: open and suspended; gorgeous on minor chords (m11)
extHint.b13: ♭13: melancholic; gives dominants a dark air
extHint.13: 13: rich and soulful; on a 7 chord it sounds like jazz and R&B

reason.sameRoot: Same root: the color changes, not the function.
reason.fromTonic: From the tonic you can go to any chord in the scale.
reason.fromTonicOutside: From the tonic anything goes, but this chord brings notes from outside the scale: it sounds like color or surprise.
reason.fifthDown: The root falls a fifth: the strongest move in harmony.
reason.susResolution: The suspended note resolves by step.
reason.preparedSus: The suspended note was already sounding: a prepared suspension.
reason.weak: No tonal rule backs this step; it may sound surprising.

lens.arrivalHint: Arrival: how natural it sounds to reach this chord from the previous one (0 to 100)
lens.clockHint: The 12 notes in a circle: the chord is a polygon; all major chords share the same rotated shape
lens.alternativesHint: What is reharmonizing? Click to see the tip
lens.susHint: Suspended chord: it lacks the third, so it hangs 'in the air'. The suspended note wants to move by step to the third.

subs.relativeHint: Shares two notes and the function: new color, same path
subs.modalInterchangeHint: The same chord in the parallel mode (major ↔ minor)
subs.tritoneSubHint: Dominant a tritone away: same tension, chromatic bass (jazz)
subs.secondaryDominantHint: Inserts this chord's dominant before it to 'push' into it
subs.susHint: Removes the third: hangs in the air, ambiguous and modern
subs.seventhHint: Adds the scale's seventh: richer and softer

help.title: Welcome to Tonalia
help.subtitle: Harmony you can see: compose and understand why it sounds that way.
help.step1: Hover to hear them, click to add them or drag them onto the ribbon. The light arcs suggest which chord sounds good next.
help.step2: Space plays. Each block's color is its function (rest, motion, tension) and its height is its tension. Select a chord to see its anatomy and alternatives.
help.step3: Open a track: the piano roll lights up the notes of the chord playing so you can choose with confidence. Turn on 'Voices' to see how chords move.
help.step4: The Library has famous progressions and 'Ear' trains your listening. View the progression as a function map or on the Tonnetz.

training.title: Ear training
training.intervalsIntro: Two notes play one after the other. How far apart are they?
training.chordsIntro: A chord plays (arpeggiated first). What kind is it?
training.functionsIntro: The tonic plays, then another chord. What function does the second chord have?
training.prompt: Listen and pick an answer (click the circle to replay)

intervals.1: One half step: the tensest rub, like a shark approaching.
intervals.2: One whole step: a scale step, natural and moving.
intervals.3: Minor third: the essence of minor, a little melancholic.
intervals.4: Major third: bright, the essence of a major chord.
intervals.5: Perfect fourth: open, sounds like a call or a fanfare.
intervals.6: Tritone: three whole steps, unstable; the heart of the dominant.
intervals.7: Perfect fifth: hollow and stable, the basis of power chords.
intervals.10: Minor seventh: bluesy, wants to move.
intervals.11: Major seventh: dreamy, a half step below the octave.
intervals.12: Octave: the same note higher; they blend.

chords.major: Major third + minor third: bright and stable.
chords.minor: Minor third + major third: dark and intimate.
chords.dim: Two minor thirds: tense, with a tritone inside.
chords.aug: Two major thirds: suspended, dreamy or mysterious.
chords.sus4: No third, a fourth instead: hangs 'in the air' waiting to resolve.
chords.sus2: No third, a second instead: open and modern.
chords.dom7: Major + minor seventh: the classic dominant, wants to resolve.
chords.maj7: Major + major seventh: soft, jazzy, sophisticated.
chords.min7: Minor + minor seventh: relaxed and warm.

functions.tonic: It sounds stable: the song could end there (vi or iii, relatives of the tonic).
functions.subdominant: It gently leaves home: motion without urgency (IV or ii).
functions.dominant: It creates tension and wants to return to the tonic (V, V7 or vii°).

tour.chooseTitle: How would you like to start?
tour.basicDesc: I'm starting from scratch: what a chord is, scales, modes, tonic and dominant… then a walk through the app.
tour.appDesc: I know the theory: just show me where things are and how the app works.
tour.chooseNote: You can replay either one from the '?' button. The theory stays in 'Learn'.
tour.introBody: First, 9 theory ideas: one per card, with a drawing and a button to hear it. Then you'll see where each idea shows up on screen. Everything stays in 'Learn' so you can review it.
tour.part2Body: You've got the ideas. Let's see where each one lives on screen and how to use it.
tour.outroBody: Try adding chords from the wheel and watch their colors. When in doubt, right-click anything. The lessons are in 'Learn' and the tour is behind the '?' button.

modulation.title: Key change
modulation.markHint: Key change: click to see how to prepare it

distanceHint.relative: Same notes, different center: a very smooth change.
distanceHint.parallel: Same tonic, different mode: the color changes, not the center.
distanceHint.neighbor: They share 6 of 7 notes: the change sounds natural.
distanceHint.close: They share {{n}} of 7 notes: you notice the change, but it flows.
distanceHint.far: They share only {{n}} notes: the change surprises; better prepare it.

planHint.pivot: A chord from both keys acts as a bridge and the dominant confirms the change.
planHint.dominant: {{v7}} is the dominant of {{key}}: it pushes straight to its tonic.
planHint.direct: No preparation: it arrives all at once, on purpose (like pop's 'up a step').

modulation.noPivot: These keys share no chords: there's no pivot. Try the dominant or the direct change.
modulation.wheelHint: Pivots light up on the wheel.
modulation.insertHint: Adds these chords at the end of the previous section, right before the change
